comments: Child denies the attribution of an object in response to MOT's question 'für wen is(t) das?' (line 4172).
Target 'alle' is used as a quantifier meaning 'all/everything' in 'alle raus', not as a negation meaning 'all gone'. Confirmed by Son's follow-up 'alles raus?'.
Child rejects mother's proposed action/interpretation of the play ('ich soll... fahr(e)n?') and replaces it with a different scenario ('...häse haben').
Child uses 'nein da' to veto or correct the placement of an object during play.
Child vetoes the mother's proposed way of lying down ('noch mal so?') and replaces it.
Child uses a negative imperative to block the action of picking up the stool from a specific location, proposing an alternative.
Child is playing 'here/gone' with an object; 'weg' indicates the object is absent/gone.
Child corrects the adult's claim that the person is not their mama by identifying them as Opa Ernst.
Child contradicts Thorsten's claim to the toy by asserting that Thorsten already has it.
Child refuses the grandfather's repeated prompts to take/play with the toy (lines 126717, 126723).
Child denies the mother's question 'is der für n Papi (1.)?' and asserts it is their own money.
Child denies the truth of the question in line 216960 regarding whether they are receiving money now.
Child resists the proposed action of moving over ('wir müssen rüber rücken').
Child responds 'nein' to mother's negative question 'wolltes(t) du gar nich(t) mehr mal(e)n?'; this agrees with the negative proposition, which is a Denial.
Child denies the mother's assertion that she has poop in her pants (line 250007).
Child asserts that items do not fit, echoing and confirming Father's claim in line 272626; Father confirms 'they are too small' in 272630.
Child reports that a toy piece does not fit in the car ('geht nicht rein'); negated fit is a claim about the world.
Child refuses to put on shoes in the context of a discussion about shoe shopping; MOT's 'doch' confirms the refusal.
Child answers Mother's question 'is(t) da ein Spiegel?' by asserting the mirror is absent.
Child reports the toy phone doesn't turn on/work, following the statement 'das is(t) kaputt'; this is a claim about the world.
Child questions the adult's claim 'schon fertig' (line 281157), contesting the fact that it is finished.
Child states the lid is gone/missing, confirming the mother's previous statement (line 281766).
Child contradicts mother's assertion in line 282477 that the animal is 'just born'.
Child states a normative rule that the dog should not have the ball in its mouth after Mother's observation; the subsequent confirmation suggests a statement of a norm.
Child makes a factual claim about the mouse's inability to eat the snail.
Child states they do not know the animal; a factual claim about knowledge.
alle is used as a quantifier meaning 'all of them' (confirmed by GIS: 'du willst alles haben?'), not as a negation meaning 'all gone'.
Child reports that a physical action (fitting a toy) is not working; negated success/fit is a claim about the world.
Child states that a toy does not fit; negated fit is a claim about the world.
Child rejects the toy piece they were struggling to fit in the preceding turns.
The child denies the mother's assertion about the child's own desire to play more ("du möchtest noch eben spielen, ja?"), which is a claim about the speaker's internal state.
Child states a preference ('don't want that') during solo play; without an explicit offer or directive, this is a claim about their own desire.
Child states they do not want to build; this is a claim about their own will rather than a refusal of a specific offer or directive to build.
Child answers mother's question 'what do you want to do?' by stating they want to do nothing; the second 'nichts' is a repetition of the first.
Child refuses the mother's request to tidy up ('einräum(e)n'), confirmed by subsequent turn 'ich will noch weiter machen'.
Child reports that something 'doesn't work' while tidying up; negated success/fit is a claim about the world.
Child reports that the toy does not fit/work while tidying up; negated fit is a claim about the world.
Child says 'hallo?' then 'nee' followed by 'hier sind keiner da', indicating the expected person on the phone is absent.
Child remarks that the shopping cart/container is empty; confirmed by mother's uptake 'alles leer'.
Child refuses the mother's request to tidy up ('räums(t) du bitte mal auf?').
Child rejects the implied placement or focus of the mother's 'guck' and replaces it with a preferred placement ('der soll da dran').
Child denies the caregiver's claim that she is a sheep ('du bist auch ein Schaf').
